items.stem: Why must human oversight be designed into many AI-enabled aerospace systems?

options.text: AI models can fail in unexpected ways, so humans provide judgment and accountability
options.rationale: Correct: oversight manages model limits and keeps accountability clear.
AI does make mistakes, which is why oversight matters.

options.text: Because humans are always slower and irrelevant
options.rationale: Oversight exists precisely because human judgment adds value.
Responsibility remains with people and organisations.

items.stem: Which TWO are sound principles for assuring AI-enabled autonomous systems? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Verify behaviour against requirements, including edge cases
options.rationale: Correct: assurance tests the system against its requirements.

options.text: Keep clear human accountability for outcomes
options.rationale: Correct: accountability must stay with people and organisations.

options.text: Assume the model is correct and skip testing

items.explanation: Correct: assurance tests the system against its requirements.

items.stem: What does a higher 'level of autonomy' generally mean for a system?

options.text: The system performs more of the task with less direct human control
options.rationale: Correct: higher autonomy shifts more decisions to the system.

options.text: The system is guaranteed to be error-free
options.rationale: Autonomy level does not guarantee correctness.

options.text: Humans have no responsibility for it
options.rationale: Responsibility remains regardless of autonomy level.

options.text: It no longer needs any requirements
options.rationale: Requirements still apply at every autonomy level.

items.explanation: Correct: higher autonomy shifts more decisions to the system.
